Economic Impact, Management, and Mitigation of Red Tides in Korea The economic consequences of red tides in Korea are significant, necessitating effective management and mitigation strategies. These harmful algal blooms (HABs) can disrupt marine ecosystems, fisheries, and aquaculture, leading to substantial financial losses. The study emphasizes the importance of monitoring and controlling toxin-producing microalgae to minimize their impact on public health and the economy. 2. Guidelines for Monitoring Toxin-Producing Microalgae Reguera et al. (2016) provide a comprehensive guide for designing and implementing monitoring plans for toxin-producing microalgae. This second edition, published by UNESCO, outlines methodologies to detect and manage harmful algal blooms, ensuring the safety of aquatic environments and public health. 3. Protecting Surface Water for Health Rickert et al. (2016) discuss strategies for identifying, assessing, and managing risks to drinking water quality in surface water catchments. Published by the World Health Organization (WHO), this work highlights the importance of safeguarding water resources to prevent waterborne diseases and ensure public health. 4. Harmful Algal Blooms and Their Impacts Rosen and St. Amand (2015) explore the occurrence and effects of harmful algal blooms, emphasizing their potential to cause human illnesses and animal deaths. The study underscores the need for effective monitoring and mitigation strategies to address these environmental and public health challenges. 5. Ecological Shifts in Lake Garda Salmaso et al. (2018) present evidence from a three-decade study in Lake Garda, demonstrating how climate change and eutrophication drive ongoing ecological shifts in large lakes. The findings highlight the interplay between environmental changes and aquatic ecosystem dynamics. 6. Microalgal Metabolites: A New Perspective Shimizu (1996) provides insights into the diverse metabolites produced by microalgae, emphasizing their ecological roles and potential applications. This work sheds light on the biochemical complexity of microalgae and their significance in aquatic ecosystems. 7. Human Health Risks from Cyanobacterial Neurotoxic Alkaloids Testai et al. (2016) review the risks to human health associated with cyanobacterial neurotoxic alkaloids, such as anatoxins and saxitoxins. The study, published in Critical Reviews in Toxicology, highlights the need for effective monitoring and risk management to protect public health. 8. Health Impacts of Ostreopsis Blooms in the Mediterranean Sea Tichadou et al. (2010) document the health effects of blooms of unicellular algae from the Ostreopsis genus along the French Mediterranean coast. The study, based on surveillance data from 2006 to 2009, identifies respiratory and dermatological symptoms in exposed individuals. 9. Human Illnesses and Animal Deaths Linked to Freshwater HABs Trevino-Garrison et al. (2015) report on cases of human illnesses and animal deaths associated with freshwater harmful algal blooms in Kansas. The study highlights the need for public awareness and preventive measures to mitigate the risks posed by these blooms. 10. Emerging Marine Biotoxins in UK Waters Turner et al. (2015) examine the potential threats posed by new or emerging marine biotoxins, such as brevetoxins, in UK waters. The study evaluates detection methodologies and emphasizes the importance of robust monitoring systems to ensure public safety. 11. Marine Algal Toxins: Origins and Health Effects Van Dolah (2000) reviews the origins, health effects, and increasing occurrence of marine algal toxins. The study underscores the need for continued research and monitoring to address the growing threat of these toxins to human and environmental health. 12. Introduction to Cyanobacteria Vidal et al. (2021) provide an overview of cyanobacteria, discussing their ecological roles and potential health risks. This work, included in the WHO publication on toxic cyanobacteria in water, serves as a foundational reference for understanding cyanobacterial blooms and their management. 13. Linking Ostreopsis Blooms to Human Health Impacts Vila et al. (2016) establish a connection between Ostreopsis cf. ovata blooms and human health impacts using ecological and epidemiological data. The study highlights the importance of interdisciplinary approaches to understanding and mitigating the effects of harmful algal blooms. 14. Effects of Rising CO2 and Global Warming on Cyanobacterial Blooms Visser et al. (2016) explore how increasing CO2 levels and global warming may stimulate harmful cyanobacterial blooms. The study emphasizes the need for proactive measures to address the environmental and public health challenges posed by climate change. 15. Fieldwork for Monitoring Cyanobacteria and Cyanotoxins Welker (2021) outlines protocols for site inspection and sampling in the context of monitoring cyanobacteria and cyanotoxins. This work, part of the WHO guidelines, provides practical guidance for fieldwork in aquatic environments. 16. Planning Monitoring Programs for Cyanobacteria Welker et al. (2021) discuss the design and implementation of monitoring programs for cyanobacteria and cyanotoxins. The study emphasizes the importance of systematic approaches to ensure the safety of water resources. 17. WHO Guidelines for Safe Recreational Water Environments The World Health Organization (2003) provides guidelines for maintaining safe recreational water environments, addressing microbial and chemical hazards to protect public health. 18. Chemical Hazards in Drinking Water WHO (2020a) highlights the risks associated with chemical contaminants in drinking water, emphasizing the need for effective monitoring and management to ensure water safety. 19. Cyanobacterial Toxins: Microcystins WHO (2020b) provides a background document on microcystins, detailing their health risks and the development of guidelines for drinking water quality and recreational water safety. 20. Cyanobacterial Toxins: Cylindrospermopsins WHO (2020c) discusses the health risks of cylindrospermopsins, providing guidance for managing these toxins in drinking and recreational water environments. 21. Cyanobacterial Toxins: Anatoxin-a and Analogues WHO (2020d) reviews the health risks of anatoxin-a and its analogues, offering recommendations for monitoring and managing these toxins in water resources. 22. Cyanobacterial Toxins: Saxitoxins WHO (2020e) examines the risks associated with saxitoxins, providing a framework for developing guidelines to protect public health. 23. Health Risks from Benthic Cyanobacteria Wood (2017) offers advice on managing health risks associated with benthic cyanobacteria, emphasizing the importance of communication strategies to raise public awareness. 24. Mitigation of Harmful Algal Blooms Using Modified Clays Yu et al. (2017) explore the use of modified clays to mitigate harmful algal blooms, discussing the underlying theory, mechanisms, and practical applications of this approach. 25. Microbial Hazards in Recreational Waters The WHO guidelines describe various microbial hazards in recreational waters, including bacteria, free-living amoebae, and helminths. The document emphasizes the importance of monitoring and controlling these hazards to protect public health. 26. Aeromonas spp. in Aquatic Environments Aeromonas species are opportunistic pathogens found in aquatic environments. They are associated with wound infections, pneumonia, and gastroenteritis, particularly during warmer months. 27. Leptospira spp. and Leptospirosis Leptospira species, transmitted through animal urine in freshwater, cause leptospirosis, a disease with a wide range of symptoms from mild to severe. Diagnosis relies on clinical suspicion and laboratory confirmation. 28. Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Recreational Waters Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a ubiquitous environmental organism, is linked to skin, ear, and eye infections following exposure to contaminated recreational water. 29. Staphylococcus aureus and Skin Infections Staphylococcus aureus is primarily associated with skin infections in recreational water users, including boils, impetigo, and folliculitis. 30. Vibrio spp. in Marine and Freshwater Environments Vibrio species, including V. vulnificus and V. parahaemolyticus, are associated with gastrointestinal and wound infections. Their prevalence is influenced by water temperature and salinity. 31. Free-Living Amoebae and Human Infections Free-living amoebae, such as Acanthamoeba and Naegleria fowleri, can cause rare but severe infections, including amoebic keratitis and primary amoebic meningoencephalitis.
